summary: Custom AI silicon was the week's biggest move: OpenAI and Broadcom unveiled 'Jalapeño', a reticle-sized inference ASIC taped out in ~9 months, while SK hynix sampled 12-high HBM4E — twin pressure points on the AI-compute/memory supply chain that three voices argued is now the real battleground. China's open-weight surge (GLM-5.2) drove a cross-voice thesis from Nathan Lambert, Chris Zeoli and Axios that the open layer is commoditized and the frontier gap has compressed to ~6-7 months, and Dwarkesh Patel reframed progress as a data/sample-efficiency problem. Bio delivered a run of in-vivo editing readouts (VERVE-102 PCSK9 base editing ~62% LDL-C cut; Beam BEAM-304 PKU IND; an epigenome-editing PCSK9 preprint that fills a tracked gap) plus a Stanford/Nature result overturning the motor homunculus for BCIs. Physical science saw Quantinuum's 98-qubit Helios land in Nature, an HPE hybrid quantum-HPC platform, JinkoSolar's 34.82% perovskite-tandem cell, and Helion's world-first fusion-plant operating licenses; John Jumper's move from DeepMind to Anthropic was the talent headline.

highlights.title: OpenAI + Broadcom unveil 'Jalapeño' custom LLM-inference ASIC
highlights.detail: OpenAI's June 24 release introduced Jalapeño, a reticle-sized inference accelerator co-developed with Broadcom from design to tape-out in ~9 months (claimed fastest-ever high-performance ASIC cycle, accelerated using OpenAI's own models); early data claims perf/watt 'substantially better' than state-of-the-art, with gigawatt-scale deployment alongside Microsoft from end-2026.

payload.claim: OpenAI + Broadcom 'Jalapeño' reticle-sized inference ASIC, design-to-tape-out in ~9 months, perf/watt 'substantially better' than SoTA, gigawatt-scale with Microsoft from end-2026.

highlights.title: OpenAI Daybreak: GPT-5.5-Cyber + Codex Security for automated patching
highlights.detail: On June 22 OpenAI expanded Daybreak, releasing GPT-5.5-Cyber (85.6% on CyberGym vs 81.8% for GPT-5.5; 39.5% vs 25.95% on ExploitGym) plus a Codex Security plugin that has scanned 30M+ commits across 30K repos, shifting the bottleneck from finding to auto-patching vulnerabilities, with Trusted Access partnerships with multiple governments.

payload.claim: OpenAI Daybreak releases GPT-5.5-Cyber (85.6% CyberGym) + Codex Security (30M+ commits / 30K repos scanned), with government Trusted Access partnerships.

highlights.title: Nobel laureate John Jumper leaves Google DeepMind for Anthropic
highlights.detail: On June 19-20 John Jumper — AlphaFold lead and 2024 Chemistry Nobel laureate — announced he is leaving Google DeepMind after ~9 years to join Anthropic, a high-profile talent move signaling intensifying competition for scientific-AI leadership.

payload.name: John Jumper
payload.role: Joining Anthropic (research) after ~9 years leading AlphaFold at Google DeepMind

highlights.title: Agon: autonomous omnidisciplinary research orchestrator ('machine scales, human steers')
highlights.detail: arXiv:2606.24177 (June 23, Youran Sun et al., Haizhao Yang group) presents Agon, a 'Prompt Economy' research orchestrator that ran 444 autonomous research loops across domains with no human-written experimental code, contributing a taxonomy separating failures the loop can self-fix from those needing human judgment.

payload.claim: Agon (arXiv:2606.24177) autonomous research orchestrator ran 444 loops across domains with no human-written experimental code.

highlights.title: Geometric Action Model (GAM) repurposes a 3D geometry foundation model for manipulation
highlights.detail: arXiv:2606.17046 (June 15; ETH Zurich/KAIST incl. Marc Pollefeys, Marco Hutter) splits a pretrained geometric foundation model to do perception, future-latent prediction and action decoding in one backbone, reporting more accurate, robust, faster and lighter contact-rich manipulation than current VLA/world-action baselines.

payload.claim: GAM (arXiv:2606.17046, ETH/KAIST) repurposes a 3D geometry foundation model for contact-rich manipulation, beating VLA/world-action baselines on accuracy, robustness, speed and size.

highlights.title: NavWM: unified navigation world model for foresight-driven planning
highlights.detail: arXiv:2606.24101 (June 23; CAS Institute of Automation + Beihang) proposes NavWM, unifying latent world reasoning, multimodal action prediction and controllable visual generation via 'latent world tokens' to combat myopic decisions and mode collapse in visual navigation.

payload.claim: NavWM (arXiv:2606.24101, CAS/Beihang) unifies latent world reasoning, action prediction and controllable generation via 'latent world tokens' for visual navigation.

highlights.title: Waymo registers German entity for European robotaxi expansion
highlights.detail: Per Bloomberg (June 25), Waymo registered 'Waymo Germany GmbH' to offer autonomous ride-hailing — an explicit step toward European market entry beyond its US footprint and prior London/Tokyo signals.

payload.new_value: Registered Waymo Germany GmbH for EU robotaxi entry (June 25 2026)
payload.previous_value: US-focused (~6 markets) plus prior intl. plans (London/Tokyo)

highlights.title: Beam's BEAM-304 in vivo base editor for PKU gets FDA IND clearance
highlights.detail: On June 18 Beam Therapeutics announced FDA IND clearance for BEAM-304, a liver-targeted LNP adenine base editor correcting PAH mutations (starting with R408W) in phenylketonuria; preclinical data normalized plasma Phe in PKU mouse models, framed as a platform/bespoke-editor program.

payload.claim: Beam BEAM-304 (in vivo LNP adenine base editor for PKU/PAH) cleared FDA IND June 18 2026; preclinical normalization of plasma Phe.

highlights.title: Nature study upends motor homunculus: whole-body signals across motor cortex
highlights.detail: A Stanford/Wu Tsai Neurosciences study (Nature, June 17; Deo, Willett, Henderson) recorded from 8 BCI-implanted participants performing 45 movements and found every motor-cortex region encodes whole-body movement, not just its canonical part — implying a single implant could control arms, communication devices and more.

payload.claim: Stanford/Nature (June 17): every motor-cortex region encodes whole-body movement (8 BCI participants, 45 movements), upending the motor homunculus and implying fewer implants for versatile BCI control.

highlights.title: Dual CD19/BCMA CAR-T drives sustained remission in systemic sclerosis (EULAR)
highlights.detail: At EULAR 2026, Yajing Zhang (Beijing GoBroad Boren Hospital) reported a dual-target CD19/BCMA CAR-T inducing sustained clinical remission in 11 refractory systemic sclerosis patients, targeting skin fibrosis and lung progression as an immune-reset strategy ahead of planned phase 2 — distinct from the tracked Autolus obe-cel lupus program.

payload.claim: Dual CD19/BCMA CAR-T (Beijing GoBroad Boren) induced sustained remission in 11 refractory systemic-sclerosis patients (EULAR 2026).

highlights.title: AlphaFold structure-mining uncovers VIPR, an ancestral pre-CRISPR system
highlights.detail: Doudna lab (UC Berkeley) used AlphaFold to hunt RAMP-like folds encoded by unrelated sequences and discovered VIPR in bacteriophages (bioRxiv, April 26; Yoon et al.). VIPR is RNA-guided but silences rather than cuts DNA; ~180 aa (~1/8 of Cas9), small enough to multiplex within one AAV vector.

payload.claim: Doudna lab used AlphaFold to discover VIPR, an RNA-guided gene-silencing system (~180 aa, ~1/8 of Cas9) in phages (bioRxiv, Yoon et al.).

highlights.title: VERVE-102 in vivo base editing: ~88% PCSK9 and ~62% LDL-C reduction (Heart-2)
highlights.detail: Phase 1b Heart-2 results for VERVE-102 (Lilly/Verve), a GalNAc-LNP in vivo adenine base editor targeting PCSK9, in 35 adults: highest dose cut PCSK9 ~88% and LDL-C ~62%, durable >1 year, with no dose-limiting toxicities. Published in NEJM.

payload.claim: VERVE-102 (Verve/Lilly) in vivo base editing cut PCSK9 ~88% and LDL-C ~62% (n=35, Heart-2), durable >1yr, no dose-limiting toxicities (NEJM).

highlights.title: In vivo epigenome editing beats nucleases for durable PCSK9 silencing (preprint)
highlights.detail: A bioRxiv preprint (March 20) reports targeted epigenetic modulation achieved the most efficient, sustained PCSK9 repression vs CRISPR/Cas9 nuclease, deaminase editing, and GalNAc-siRNA, using mRNA editors in Arcturus LUNAR LNPs in mice — flagging epigenome editing as a scarless durable in-vivo silencing route.

payload.claim: bioRxiv preprint: in vivo epigenome editing gave the most durable PCSK9 silencing vs nuclease/deaminase editing and siRNA (mRNA editors in Arcturus LUNAR LNPs, mice).

highlights.title: Sandia + Quantinuum publish 98-qubit Helios results in Nature
highlights.detail: A peer-reviewed Nature paper (June 17) reports Quantinuum's 98-qubit trapped-ion Helios at 99.9975% single-qubit and 99.921% two-qubit fidelity plus 99.967% SPAM; Sandia certified it operates beyond classical simulation — a key step toward fault tolerance.

payload.claim: Quantinuum 98-qubit Helios (Nature, June 17): 99.9975% 1q / 99.921% 2q fidelity, 99.967% SPAM; Sandia certified beyond-classical operation.

highlights.title: HPE launches hybrid quantum-HPC platform integrating Quantinuum + IQM
highlights.detail: At HPE Discover (June 15-18), HPE unveiled a hybrid classical-quantum platform integrating multiple qubit modalities with Cray supercomputing; Quantinuum announced a quantum-HPC collaboration and IQM (already tracked) contributed superconducting QPU tech live at Oak Ridge — pushing quantum-classical hybrid orchestration toward enterprise deployment.

payload.claim: HPE's hybrid quantum-HPC platform (HPE Discover, June 15-18) integrates Quantinuum + IQM QPUs with Cray supercomputing for enterprise quantum-classical workflows.

highlights.title: JinkoSolar hits certified 34.82% perovskite-silicon tandem cell
highlights.detail: JinkoSolar announced (June 19) a 34.82% certified efficiency for an N-type TOPCon perovskite-silicon tandem cell (certified by SIMIT/Chinese Academy of Sciences), up from its own 34.76% and just behind LONGi's 34.85% record — continued tandem march past the single-junction limit.

payload.claim: JinkoSolar: 34.82% certified perovskite-silicon tandem cell (SIMIT-certified), up from 34.76%, near LONGi's 34.85% record.

highlights.title: Helion secures world-first regulatory licenses for a fusion power plant
highlights.detail: Helion received what it calls the world's first regulatory licenses for a commercial fusion plant (Washington State radioactive-materials and air-emissions licenses, June 19-23), enabled by NRC's byproduct-material framework (2024 ADVANCE Act); clears earthwork on the Orion plant in Malaga, WA targeting 50 MW+ for Microsoft. Distinct from the tracked $465M Series G.

payload.claim: Helion received world-first regulatory licenses (WA radioactive-materials + air-emissions) for its Orion commercial fusion plant; enabled by NRC byproduct-material framework (ADVANCE Act).

highlights.title: SK hynix ships 12-layer HBM4E samples ahead of schedule
highlights.detail: SK hynix (June 17) began sampling 12-high HBM4E to major customers: 16 Gbps/pin, 48 GB per stack, >20% better power efficiency and +17% heat resistance vs HBM4 — addressing the memory wall for next-gen AI accelerators (e.g., NVIDIA Vera Rubin class).

payload.claim: SK hynix sampling 12-high HBM4E (16 Gbps/pin, 48 GB/stack, >20% better power, +17% heat resistance vs HBM4) for next-gen AI accelerators.

highlights.title: CFS publishes 5 peer-reviewed papers validating ARC power-plant physics
highlights.detail: Commonwealth Fusion Systems (June 4) published five peer-reviewed papers in a special issue of the Journal of Plasma Physics laying out the physics basis for its ARC plant to deliver ~400 MW net electricity, building on SPARC learnings (grid electricity targeted early 2030s).

payload.claim: CFS published 5 peer-reviewed papers (Journal of Plasma Physics) on the ARC plant's physics basis for ~400 MW net electricity.

highlights.title: Type One Energy names ex-BP CEO Bernard Looney to board
highlights.detail: Type One Energy (June 16) appointed former BP CEO Bernard Looney as an independent director as it closes its Series B and begins procurement for its Infinity One stellarator prototype at TVA's Bull Run site — bringing major-energy capital/project-delivery expertise to the stellarator race.

payload.name: Bernard Looney
payload.role: Independent director, Type One Energy (former CEO, BP)

highlights.title: China's open-weight models have commoditized the open layer; frontier gap ~6-7 months
highlights.detail: Three independent voices argued this week that GLM-5.2 marks an inflection: China supplies the majority of open-model tokens and the US-China lag has compressed to ~6-9 months, shifting strategic value from 'who trains the best model' to 'who supplies the tokens the world runs.'

payload.thesis: Chinese open-weight models (GLM-5.2, Kimi, Qwen, DeepSeek) have commoditized the open-model layer and closed the gap to the closed frontier to ~6-7 months, shifting value to compute/memory and distribution rather than the model.
examples: Nathan Lambert (Interconnects, Jun 22): GLM-5.2 is the first open-weight model that 'feels right' as a general coding agent; gap to Opus 4.5 ~204 days.
Chris Zeoli (Data Gravity, Jun 24): Chinese open models ~61% of OpenRouter tokens by May 2026; 4 of top 5 used models are Chinese.
Axios (Jun 23): GLM-5.2 reignited the China-gap debate; David Sacks cites a 6-9 month US lead.

highlights.title: Dwarkesh Patel: data, not algorithms, is the 'black hole' driving AI
highlights.detail: In a widely shared June 19 essay, Patel argues the real driver of AI progress is a bespoke data engine (expert RL trajectories, rubrics), not architecture — which is why open labs catch up within months by distilling from APIs — and frames a ~million-fold human sample-efficiency gap that scaling alone cannot close.

payload.thesis: Data (and the compute to generate/curate it) is the dominant driver of AI progress, not architecture; models remain thousands-to-millions of times less sample-efficient than humans and scaling parameters can't close that gap.
examples: Open models lag closed by only ~4 months (Epoch) because data distills easily from public APIs.
Humans see ~200M language tokens to adulthood vs tens of trillions for frontier models.
Chinchilla math: infinite parameters cut required data only ~10x, far short of the human gap.

highlights.title: Chris Zeoli (Data Gravity) — infra-investor field maps that quantify the AI stack
highlights.detail: Zeoli's June 24 'China's Open-Weight Takeover' is a rigorously sourced field map of the Chinese AI ecosystem (token share, lab valuations, HBM bottlenecks) that crystallized the week's biggest debate; he writes from an infra-investor lens on the economics layer of AI.

payload.name: Chris Zeoli
payload.focus: AI infrastructure, compute/memory supply chains, model-market economics, China AI ecosystem
payload.notes: Substack 'Data Gravity' — data-dense, well-cited analyses (OpenRouter token data, lab valuations, HBM constraints); strong on the economics layer rather than model research.

highlights.title: Duke & IonQ entangle three remote trapped-ion nodes (first multi-node GHZ)
highlights.detail: On June 20 a Duke/IonQ team (Monroe group) demonstrated tripartite GHZ entanglement across three spatially separated barium-ion nodes linked by photonic interconnects, with no local two-qubit gates or post-selection, at 84-88% fidelity — a step toward modular, networked quantum computers (also closing a Mermin-test detection loophole).

highlights.title: PNNL, Nvidia & Fervo to build a public AI 'digital twin' of geothermal reservoirs
highlights.detail: Announced June 22, the partnership will train AI on Fervo's Nevada/Utah well data to build the Enhanced Geothermal System Twin — a public, real-time subsurface model (via Nvidia Omniverse) to optimize drilling and water injection and cut geothermal guesswork.

highlights.title: JinkoSolar — tandem-cell record contender (entity reconciliation)
highlights.detail: Top-tier Chinese PV manufacturer behind this week's 34.82% certified perovskite-silicon tandem cell; not previously tracked despite being a primary driver of the tandem-efficiency race alongside the tracked LONGi.

payload.name: JinkoSolar
payload.why: One of the world's largest solar manufacturers and a perovskite-silicon tandem record contender (34.82% certified, June 2026); key player pushing tandem cells past the single-junction limit toward mass production.

highlights.title: Type One Energy — stellarator commercialization player (entity reconciliation)
highlights.detail: Stellarator fusion company building the Infinity One prototype at TVA's Bull Run site; just added ex-BP CEO Bernard Looney to its board and closing a Series B. Not previously tracked despite being a leading stellarator-path competitor.

payload.name: Type One Energy
payload.why: Leading stellarator-path fusion developer (Infinity One prototype at TVA Bull Run, grid power targeted ~2034); closing Series B, recruiting major-energy leadership (Bernard Looney) — a key non-tokamak competitor to track.
